Overview

A compact, open mobile base for robots that need to get around.

Luchs A gives your robot a reliable pair of legs. It carries up to 80 kg, steers all four wheels, and talks to your computer over standard industrial interfaces. Mount your sensors and payload on the top rails, plug into the expansion bay, and start building the application instead of the drivetrain.

  • Four drive configurations, one platform. Skid-steer, front Ackermann, dual Ackermann or full four-wheel steering. The main body is shared; only the drive module changes.
  • Open by design. CAN, RS-485 and RS-232 control, a published protocol, and ROS 2 software with an SDK, robot model and simulator in the box.
  • Power for your payload. 48 V / 10 A and 12 V / 8 A outputs, each with over-current, short-circuit and over-temperature protection.
  • Safety you don't have to add later. Dual emergency stops, ultrasonic collision stop, power-on self-test and a monitored battery.

Motion

Moves the way your task needs.

The A-4WS supports all four motion models below and switches between them on a single command. Your planner can use whichever model suits it, and the reported odometry follows the model you selected.

Crab walk

All four wheels point the same way, so the chassis slides sideways or diagonally without turning its nose.

A-4WS

Pivot turn

The chassis spins about its own centre. Ideal for narrow aisles and docking.

All configurations

Skid-steer

Wheels stay straight; the chassis turns by driving the left and right sides at different speeds.

All configurations

Ackermann

Front wheels steer like a car. Smooth, predictable arcs that are gentle on tyres and floors.

A-FA · A-DA · A-4WS

Dual Ackermann

Front and rear axles steer in opposite directions, halving the turning radius.

A-DA · A-4WS
Design

Simple outside. Serviceable inside.

A carbon-steel and aluminium frame with independent suspension at every corner. The A-4WS sits on swing-arm suspension with 220 mm of ground clearance; the other configurations use double wishbones front and rear.

Autonomy by TerraAgent Robotics

The autonomy is ours.
Built by TAR, for the Luchs family.

RJ Tech builds the chassis. TerraAgent Robotics (TAR) turns it into a robot that does your job: we integrate the sensors and the computer, set up positioning and navigation, and adapt the software to your site. The building blocks are shared across the Luchs family and already run on real vehicles, on real data.

01 What we deliver

Navigation kit

Built-in computer with ROS pre-installed, LiDAR-based SLAM (GMapping and Cartographer) and the ROS navigation stack.

  • Live mapping, online and offline
  • Global and local path planning
  • Dynamic obstacle avoidance and trajectory tracking

Sensor integration

We mount, wire and calibrate the sensors your application needs, using the deck rails and the protected power outputs.

  • Single-line LiDAR and depth cameras
  • IMU and wheel-encoder fusion
  • Custom masts and payload brackets

Application engineering

From a first demo to a pilot fleet: we help you define the task, adapt the software, and test it where the robot will actually work.

  • Mission setup and tuning
  • Data logging and visualisation
  • Training and handover

Real-vehicle tiles show our own software running on real vehicles. Off-road tiles are our perception model run offline on recorded off-road driving data. Planning tiles are replays of our planning stack. All are building blocks we integrate on the Luchs family.

Integration

Bolt it on. Plug it in. Drive it from code.

Mounting rails

Two 2040 aluminium extrusions, 700 mm long at 200 mm centres, take standard 40-series slot nuts and brackets. Mount sensor masts, robot arms, lifting modules or cargo boxes without drilling the chassis.

Expansion bay

Under a magnetic cover at the rear of the deck: one DB9 signal connector (CAN, RS-485, RS-232) and one power connector with 48 V / 10 A and 12 V / 8 A outputs.

External or built-in computer

Connect your own industrial PC or edge computer to the expansion bay, or order the built-in computer with HDMI, USB 2.0 and Ethernet ports on the chassis.

Software that's ready on day one

The ROS 2 driver takes cmd_vel and publishes odometry, joint states, chassis and safety state, battery data and diagnostics, with watchdogs and limits built in. A C++ SDK, a command-line tool and a built-in simulator let you start before the chassis arrives. The full CAN and serial protocols are documented if you prefer to write your own.

Safety

Layered protection, built in.

Safety on Luchs A doesn't depend on your software being right. The chassis watches itself, and the most important protections work at the hardware level.

Two emergency stops

One on each side. A press cuts motion commands, brakes the motors and locks the chassis until it is reset.

Ultrasonic collision stop

In remote-control mode the chassis brakes if an obstacle comes within 20 cm. In automatic mode the ranges are reported to your software.

Power-on self-test

Checks the battery, power rails, communication links, drive motors and ultrasonic sensors before the chassis will move.

Battery management

The BMS protects against over-charge, over-discharge, over-current and abnormal temperature.

Charging interlock

With the charger plugged in, the drive is disabled and the chassis ignores all motion commands.

Protected outputs

Every power channel is current-monitored with software cut-off; critical outputs add hardware protection against overload, short circuit and over-temperature.

Remote control

The handheld transmitter drives the chassis. It can hand control to your computer at the flick of a switch, and take it back just as quickly.

Maintenance

Motion is locked out. Used to clear faults, reset after an emergency stop, or release the brakes to push the chassis by hand.

Automatic

Your computer drives over CAN, RS-485 or RS-232. The light bar turns blue so everyone nearby knows who's in charge.

Appendix

Terms and abbreviations

4WDFour-wheel drive: every wheel has its own drive motor.
4WSFour-wheel steering: every wheel can be steered on its own.
Ackermann steeringCar-style steering in which the inner wheel turns more sharply than the outer one, so both follow the same arc.
BMSBattery Management System: electronics that monitor and protect the battery.
CANController Area Network: a robust two-wire bus widely used in vehicles and machines.
Crab walkSideways or diagonal travel with all wheels pointing the same way.
DB9A 9-pin D-subminiature connector.
IP33 / IP54Ingress Protection rating to IEC 60529. IP33: protected against objects over 2.5 mm and spraying water. IP54: dust-protected and protected against splashing water.
LiFePO4Lithium iron phosphate: a lithium-ion chemistry known for long cycle life and thermal stability.
OdometryAn estimate of the robot's motion computed from wheel speeds and steering angles.
Pivot turnTurning on the spot about the chassis centre; turning radius 0 m.
ROSRobot Operating System: the most widely used open-source robotics middleware.
RS-232 / RS-485Serial communication standards. RS-485 is differential and suited to longer, noisier cable runs.
Skid-steerSteering by driving the left and right wheels at different speeds; also called differential drive.
SLAMSimultaneous Localisation and Mapping: building a map while working out where the robot is on it.
